items.title: CMake references a resource with the wrong filename case

findings.title: Case mismatch for Resources/Images/banner.jpg vs Banner.jpg breaks builds on case-sensitive filesystems
findings.explanation: `MyocardialPerfusionImaging/CMakeLists.txt` lists `Resources/Images/banner.jpg` (lowercase `b`) in `MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES`, and `MyocardialPerfusionImaging/MyocardialPerfusionImaging.py` line 50 looks up `Resources/Images/banner.jpg`. However, the file committed in the repository is `MyocardialPerfusionImaging/Resources/Images/Banner.jpg` (uppercase `B`). On case-sensitive filesystems (such as Linux, where Slicer extensions are built and packaged on the Linux factory), CMake's `slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule` will fail to find `Resources/Images/banner.jpg` during configuration/installation, breaking the Linux build.
findings.suggestion: Rename `MyocardialPerfusionImaging/Resources/Images/Banner.jpg` to `MyocardialPerfusionImaging/Resources/Images/banner.jpg` (or update both `MyocardialPerfusionImaging/CMakeLists.txt` and `MyocardialPerfusionImaging/MyocardialPerfusionImaging.py` to match the exact filename case).

findings.title: CMake references a resource with the wrong filename case
findings.explanation: The available repository listing contains Resources/Images/Banner.jpg, not banner.jpg. On case-sensitive filesystems the build macro cannot find the listed banner resource, preventing the extension from building or packaging; the hub also looks for the lowercase name.
findings.suggestion: Rename the file to banner.jpg or consistently change both the CMake entry and runtime path to the actual filename; verify a Linux build.

claude.reason: CMakeLists.txt:25-29 lists Resources/Images/banner.jpg and Resources/Images/logo.png. The directory listing shows only Resources/Images/Banner.jpg (capital B), and no logo.png at all. On case-sensitive Linux build machines both resources are missing, so the scripted-module build/install step will fail. MyocardialPerfusionImaging.py:50 also uses the lowercase name. The issue is larger than the case mismatch: logo.png is absent too.

gpt.reason: MyocardialPerfusionImaging/CMakeLists.txt:25-34 lists 'Resources/Images/banner.jpg' as a resource supplied to the build macro, but the repository listing shows only 'Resources/Images/Banner.jpg'. On case-sensitive systems the specified input is absent, breaking the scripted-module build/package; CMake also lists missing 'Resources/Images/logo.png'. MyocardialPerfusionImaging/MyocardialPerfusionImaging.py:49-50 likewise references the lowercase banner. I could not run the build or inspect the Slicer macro implementation.

gemini.reason: `MyocardialPerfusionImaging/CMakeLists.txt:25-29` lists `Resources/Images/banner.jpg` (lowercase `b`) and `Resources/Images/logo.png` in `MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES`, and `MyocardialPerfusionImaging/MyocardialPerfusionImaging.py:50` looks up `Resources/Images/banner.jpg`. In the repository, `MyocardialPerfusionImaging/Resources/Images/` contains `Banner.jpg` (uppercase `B`) and does not contain `logo.png` at all. On case-sensitive filesystems (Linux build factory) and for the missing `logo.png` on all platforms, `slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule` (`ctkMacroCompilePythonScript`) will fail to copy/install the missing resources.

items.title: DICOM scene export can file unrelated patient data under one patient

findings.title: DICOM scene export can file unrelated patient data under one patient
findings.evidence:
def exportScene(folder):
    """The whole scene as a Slicer Data Bundle DICOM file in folder. Returns ([path], reference node or None, added
    to the database)."""
    import DICOMLib
    slicer = _slicer()
    tags, fileName, reference = exportTags()
findings.explanation: The exporter packs the entire Slicer scene but selects one reference patient's DICOM identity. The mixed-patient scan in case.py explicitly excludes studies assigned role None, whereas those nodes remain in the scene. If an unrelated patient's study is present or excluded, exporting the scene and sending it from the DICOM browser can disclose that patient's images and identifiers inside a bundle filed under the selected patient, without a specific warning about the excluded data.
findings.suggestion: Export a patient-scoped scene or inspect all scene contents, including excluded and unidentifiable nodes, and block or obtain explicit informed confirmation before writing a mixed-patient DICOM bundle.

claude.reason: dicomexport.py:389-409 exports the whole scene as a Slicer Data Bundle under the reference study's tags. That is the user's own loaded scene, saved only after the user clicks Save > Scene as DICOM. The report dialog (_report, ~445-455) says which patient and study it was filed under. Mixing in another patient's data would require the user to have loaded it, and nothing is sent out automatically. This is a possible data-labelling pitfall, not a concrete path to harm, so it is not blocking safety.

gpt.reason: MyocardialPerfusionImaging/MyocardialPerfusionImagingLib/dicomexport.py:389-406 calls 'exportTags()' and 'DICOMLib.DICOMExportScene(fileName, work)' to export the entire scene under a single reference; lines 56-61 describe the whole scene as a private-tag bundle filed under the MPI patient's study. case.py:159-168 excludes role None from the patient scan, and case.py:243-245 advises setting another patient's volumes to None. Those volumes remain in the scene; if the user subsequently sends the bundle via the DICOM browser, unrelated patient data may be disclosed under the wrong identity. The tooltip says whole scene, but does not specifically warn that excluded patients remain included. The Slicer DICOM exporter implementation and an actual export were not available to inspect.

gemini.reason: `MyocardialPerfusionImaging/MyocardialPerfusionImagingLib/dicomexport.py:389-409` uses `DICOMLib.DICOMExportScene` to export the entire Slicer scene (`slicer.mrmlScene`) as a Slicer Data Bundle (`sdbFile`) tagged with the reference patient's DICOM attributes (`exportTags()`). Meanwhile, `MyocardialPerfusionImaging/MyocardialPerfusionImagingLib/case.py:166-168` skips studies with `study.role == studiesLib.EXCLUDED_ROLE` (`None`), and `case.py:244-245` instructs the user to "set the volumes of another patient to None in Data roles", leaving those nodes in the scene where `exportScene` (as well as `saveSceneBundle`) will include them in the exported scene bundle. Note that `dicomexport.py:56-59` explicitly documents in the UI tooltip that "Save scene as DICOM Packs the whole Slicer scene", which is how Slicer's built-in `DICOMExportScene` works, though the advice in `case.py:244-245` to exclude another patient's volume by setting its role to `None` rather than removing it from the scene is a minor usability/design caveat rather than a blocking security issue.

items.title: Second-monitor screenshot can overwrite an existing file without confirmation

findings.title: Second-monitor screenshot can overwrite an existing file without confirmation
findings.explanation: The save dialog only selects and checks the first path. When a second monitor window is captured, the automatically constructed _2.png path can already exist, and saving it overwrites that unrelated prior screenshot without an overwrite confirmation.
findings.suggestion: Check every generated output path before writing and ask before replacing any existing file, or use collision-free filenames.

claude.reason: dicomexport.py:545-550 writes {root}_2.png without checking whether it exists. The Qt save dialog only confirms overwrite of the first path. The overwritten file is a user-chosen screenshot name with a numeric suffix, so this is an ordinary minor bug, not a safety blocker.

gpt.reason: MyocardialPerfusionImaging/MyocardialPerfusionImagingLib/dicomexport.py:531-550 asks for one path, then uses 'target = path if number == 1 else f"{root}_{number}.png"' and 'image.save(target, "PNG")' without checking whether the derived paths already exist. With a second monitor capture an existing _2.png can be overwritten without confirmation, a concrete path to unintended user-file destruction. Lines 326-337 confirm additional visible monitor windows are included; the exact Qt runtime behavior was not tested.

gemini.reason: In `MyocardialPerfusionImaging/MyocardialPerfusionImagingLib/dicomexport.py:534-551`, `saveScreenshot()` prompts for `path` via `QFileDialog.getSaveFileName` (defaulting to a timestamped name `Tarvos_{caseLabel()}_{stamp()}.png`) and then writes any additional Monitor 2 window capture to `f"{root}_{number}.png"` (`dicomexport.py:548-549`) without a second overwrite prompt. Because the default filename includes a second-granularity timestamp (`%Y%m%d_%H%M%S`, `dicomexport.py:166`), an overwrite would only happen if a user manually chose an existing base name where `{root}_2.png` already existed. This is a minor UX detail, not a blocking safety issue.

findings.title: Gated segmentation runs synchronously without per-frame progress
findings.evidence:
for label, node in gates:
            array = slicer.util.arrayFromVolume(node).astype(np.float32)
            matrix = worldToIjk(node, self.study)
            spacing = node.GetSpacing()
            try:
                # on the gate masked like the static volume the wall was detected on (liver and gut out)
                result = wallLib.fitGate(sampler(array, matrix, mask, center), staticResult, params)
findings.explanation: The UI's show() calls gatedStudy().build() synchronously, fitting and reslicing each frame before returning to the event loop. For large gated sequences the interface can appear frozen, with no per-frame progress or cancellation.
findings.suggestion: Move computation off the GUI thread where safe, or provide responsive per-frame progress and cancellation.

items.title: Module directory is inserted into the shared Python import path

findings.title: Module directory is inserted into the shared Python import path
findings.explanation: Loading the extension changes import precedence for the whole Slicer process, including other extensions, and can cause name collisions if another module uses the same top-level names.
findings.suggestion: Use Slicer's normal module paths and uniquely named packages without prepending to sys.path, where possible.

items.title: Regional EF tooltip misstates the default reference

findings.title: Regional EF tooltip misstates the default reference
findings.evidence:
"rings into wedges from the long axis out to the endocardium, between the valve plane and the LV "
            "center (so a basal wedge also shrinks as the valve plane descends), and on the apex into cones from "
            "the LV center. Floating (default): every frame's own LV center and epicardial apex, since with a "
            "fixed center a heart that moves as a whole makes the wedges on one side grow and on the other shrink "
            "(a 4 mm shift changes them by tens of %). Fixed: the static fit's LV center and axis. Myocardium mass "
findings.explanation: DEFAULT_EF_REFERENCE is actually 'fixed', and the combo selects that constant. A user relying on the tooltip may believe whole-heart motion is removed when the selected fixed reference instead incorporates that motion into regional EF.
findings.suggestion: Align the displayed default, the constant, and the documented interpretation.

items.title: Toolbar and MRML scene observers are installed globally at Slicer startup

findings.title: Toolbar and MRML scene observers are installed globally at Slicer startup
findings.explanation: Every module in this extension (`MyocardialPerfusionImaging.py` and the step modules) connects `_installToolbar` to `startupCompleted()`, which instantiates `WorkflowToolbar` (`MyocardialPerfusionImagingLib/toolbar.py` lines 278-324) at Slicer startup for all users, even if the user never opens the Myocardial Perfusion Imaging module. While the toolbar hides itself when another module is active, `WorkflowToolbar.__init__` also attaches persistent `EndCloseEvent` and `EndImportEvent` observers to `slicer.mrmlScene` that call `resetToStart()`. `resetToStart()` creates/modifies a singleton `vtkMRMLScriptedModuleNode` (`MPISession`) in the scene on every scene import or close across the entire Slicer session. Creating toolbar widgets and scene observers should be deferred until the user actually enters the module.
findings.suggestion: Install the workflow toolbar and register scene observers lazily when `MyocardialPerfusionImagingWidget.enter()` (or `setup()`) is first called rather than on Slicer's `startupCompleted()` signal.
